scenarios.title: Soiled face turned away from the spray source
scenarios.test: A dessert plate with oven-dried egg yolk on its eating face standing upright in the wide gap of the rear rows of the lower basket: face to the arm axis (A) against turned round in the same place (B). Beside it, the plate as the loading physics seats it in R1 slot 5: facing the axis (C), and put in reversed and left to settle (D)
scenarios.adapted: A porcelain dessert plate stands in for the dinner plate. A and B are set poses: the plate stands exactly upright (no lean) about 56 mm right of the arm axis, where the tines lean apart and leave room for it either way round; the runner checks that it cuts into nothing. In a slot between tines the same plate cannot simply be turned round: the tines lean outwards, the seated plate faces the axis tipped up with the tines. The pair of the first build that compared the seated plate with one put in reversed is gone: on the present basket the loader does not seat a reversed plate in that slot, and the seated plate turned round in place cuts 2 mm into the tines.

scenarios.title: Plate pitch too small
scenarios.test: Rows of IEC dinner plates with egg yolk in the rear lane of the lower basket: two to a slot half a pitch apart (about 9 mm from plate to plate, B), one per slot (18.25 mm, A), every second slot (36.5 mm, C); the plate at slot 6 is scored on its upper half (in B the one of the pair whose face is covered by the other)
scenarios.adapted: The tines of the Bosch fix the pitch at 18.25 mm, so the checklist's 12, 20 and 30 mm become half a pitch, every slot and every second slot. Seven plates per row (eight when crowded). A and C are settled by the loading physics between the tines. B cannot be: a slot is 14 mm wide, two plates in it nest (the covered well under 1 mm from its partner's back over its whole area: a contact, not a narrow gap; found by the review of 11 October 2026), and a plate half a pitch in front of a seated one stands in the next tine. For B the tines of the rear lane are folded down and the row is set from the seat the physics gave the plate behind in slot 6: the covered plate of every pair stands at that seat, two slots along per pair, its partner parallel to it half a pitch (9.1 mm) in front, and the whole row is raised by the 11 mm at which it clears the folded tines; the covered well then looks into a gap of 3.7 to 5 mm. So B differs from A by the pitch, by 11 mm of height and by the tines, which in A stand in front of the foot of every plate.
scenarios.stages: water: jets (gap geometry), run-off; soil: removal laws

tierNote: This is a fast wash, a preview of the official one (coarser surfaces, fewer droplets). Measured on this programme with anchored-v7.owner-capsule (the careful standard load, level seeds 1 and 2, simulation seeds 1 to 4), its verdict on a soiled item differs from the official wash in 11 of 100 cases: 0 in 100 for crockery, 23 in 100 for cutlery, 5 in 100 for glass, 0 in 100 for melamine. Scores are counted on the official wash.
